title: Jobs of the Future
paragraphs: The world of work is changing fast. According to the World Economic Forum, by 2030 many jobs that exist today will disappear — replaced by artificial intelligence and automation. At the same time, millions of completely new jobs will be created.

Some experts believe that over 60% of children starting primary school today will work in jobs that do not yet exist. This sounds alarming, but it is also exciting. It means the most important skill for the future is not a specific technical skill — it is the ability to adapt and keep learning.

In Kazakhstan, the government has identified several key sectors for future employment: technology (IT, data science, cybersecurity), healthcare, green energy, finance, and education. Young people who gain skills in these areas will have strong career prospects.

At WKU, students are encouraged to think about their future careers early. Dr. Akhmetov runs workshops called 'Future Ready'. He asks students to think not just about what job they want, but about what skills they will need and how they will develop them.

Amir Bekzhanov dreams of becoming a software engineer. Kamila Seitkali wants to work in international education. Zhibek hopes to start her own business. 'The future belongs to those who prepare for it,' says Dr. Akhmetov. 'Don't just study for your exams — study for your life.'

One thing is certain: in the future, communication skills, emotional intelligence, and the ability to work in teams will be just as important as technical expertise. The WKU English programme is designed to help students develop all of these skills.

dialogue.text: That sounds perfect for the future! Have you done any internships yet?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Not yet, but I plan to apply for a summer internship at a tech company in Almaty.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I hope to work in international education. I want to make learning more accessible.
